title: 1992 AHSME Problem 30
statement: Let \(ABCD\) be an isosceles trapezoid with bases \(AB=92\) and \(CD=19.\) Suppose \(AD=BC=x\) and a circle with center on \(\overline{AB}\) is tangent to segments \(\overline{AD}\) and \(\overline{BC}.\) If \(m\) is the smallest possible value of \(x,\) then \(m^2=\)

solutions.text:
Place \(A=(-46,0),\) \(B=(46,0),\) \(D=(-\frac{19}{2},h),\) and \(C=(\frac{19}{2},h).\) Symmetry forces the circle’s center to be \(O=(0,0).\) The horizontal offset along each leg is \(\frac{73}{2},\) so \[ x^2=h^2+\left(\frac{73}{2}\right)^2. \] The perpendicular from \(O\) to a leg first has its foot on the segment when the foot reaches the upper endpoint; this boundary condition is \(OD\perp AD.\) Thus \[ \begin{aligned} (-\frac{19}{2},h)\cdot(\frac{73}{2},h)&=0,\\ h^2&=\frac{1387}{4}. \end{aligned} \] Therefore \[ m^2=\frac{1387+5329}{4}=1679. \]

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: By symmetry, place the trapezoid with its bases centered on the same vertical axis and put the circle’s center at the midpoint of \(AB\)
Write the distance from the center to a leg and require the tangency point to lie on the leg segment; the minimum occurs at an endpoint case
